_readme: Every rule the calculators apply lives here, with the official text it was read in on retrieved_at. Data figures (premiums, nonrenewals, claims, indexes) live in national.json, states.json and public/data, built by scripts/build-data.py from the Treasury workbook, the Census relationship file and BLS series.

data._basis: Treasury FIO workbook, tab 'Disclaimer & Background': ZIP codes with at least 10 reporting insurers and at least 50 policies; HO-3 and HO-5 policies; 80 percent of those policies nationwide by direct premiums written; residual market plans, excess and surplus lines, flood and 2023-2024 not included. Report p. 13, Figure 8 note: Texas insurer data did not include nonrenewals.

escrow._basis: 12 CFR 1024.17(c)(1)(i)-(ii): monthly escrow deposit of one-twelfth of the annual disbursements plus a cushion of no more than one-sixth of the estimated annual disbursements; 1024.17(f)(3)(ii): a shortage of one month's payment or more may be spread in equal monthly payments over at least 12 months.

florida._basis: Fla. Stat. 627.701(3)(a): hurricane deductible options of $500, 2, 5 and 10 percent of the dwelling limit must be offered; 627.701(5)(a)1: the hurricane deductible applies once per calendar year to all hurricane losses with the same insurer or group. Fla. Stat. 627.4133(2)(a)-(b): 45 days' notice of the renewal premium, 120 days' notice of nonrenewal (10 days for nonpayment). Fla. Stat. 627.351(6)(c)5.a: a primary residence offered comparable private coverage is not eligible for Citizens unless that premium is more than 20 percent above Citizens.

coinsurance._basis: Common replacement cost condition of standard homeowners forms (replacement cost paid when the dwelling limit is at least 80 percent of the full replacement cost, otherwise a proportional amount or actual cash value), described in our words; the calculator lets the reader change the percentage written in their own policy.
